coverage: Whole image once for layout; half a once line by line against C and H: date, salutation, all eight body lines including clipped ends, all accents/punctuation/reference digits/capitals, cancelled tail, and closing. Half b once: blank lower field and handwritten archival 12. All margins inspected; no signature, display, diagram or drawing found. Fifteen unresolved loci received one tight crop and one inspection each. No part remains unviewed; no OCR, external research, other page or other reader was used.

changes.evidence: Crop 01: her is intact; only the separated upper and lower right terminals of the initial survive. C is supported, but its left curve is absent. H marks a supplied initial; the retained doubt is not a claim that H misread a complete letter.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.evidence: Crop 02: after que, the copied right boundary leaves two tiny dark fragments, without a readable complete letter or word. H explicitly restores tu; those two letters cannot be verified from this image.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.evidence: Crop 03: e is complete and a right shoulder/upright survives before it; the first letter has lost its left side. The probable n remains doubtful rather than a certain restoration.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 2, first accent of envoyé
changes.evidence: Crop 04: a distinct dark mark lies above the initial e, with an upper segment and a descending right segment. A grave-like mark is favoured; the degraded angle also permits circumflex. Plain unaccented e is no longer retained. The final acute over é is clear.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 2, right edge after cela
changes.evidence: Crop 05: a is complete; one following top serif and upright survive at the right boundary, without the rest of that glyph or word. They do not distinguish u/n/r or establish the letters supplied by H.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 3, clipped initial of permis
changes.evidence: Crop 06: ermis is legible. A right-hand bowl and lower fragment of the first letter remain at the boundary; its left stem and descender are substantially lost. Retain the probable p with doubt.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 3, first letter of le after imprimeur
changes.evidence: Crop 14: the first glyph has a tall l-like serifed upright together with a rounded lower contour extending to both sides. A c/l or e/l superposition is possible; the inner crossbar and strike order are not secure. A single degraded d is also a visible-shape alternative. Neither witness marks this locus. The alternatives preserve uncertainty about both letter identity and correction state.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 4, clipped initial of SGA
changes.evidence: Crop 07: G and A are legible ordinary capitals; only right-hand upper/lower portions of the preceding capital survive. S is probable but not completely available. No mathematical alphabet or boldface is evidenced.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 4, clipped end after mainte
changes.evidence: Crop 08: mainte ends at the copied right boundary. No following n, a, n, t or comma is available. H supplies a continuation and punctuation; neither is silently imported.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 5, clipped elle and following cancelled tail
changes.evidence: Crop 09: the clipped initial and dense contours support elle only tentatively. Immediately afterward are two conspicuous x-shaped cancellation strikes over a short tail. The covered letters cannot be stably separated. H omits the cancellation; no definite earlier character or strike order is invented.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 6, clipped initial of qu’elle
changes.evidence: Crop 10: u’elle is intact; the preceding clipped glyph retains a descending right side consistent with q, while its left bowl is absent. Keep the probable reading with doubt.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 7, clipped initial of Cela
changes.evidence: Crop 11: ela is clear; two separated terminal fragments of the preceding capital remain at the edge. C is supported, but its missing left curve prevents a wholly seen letter.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.evidence: Crop 12: fasci and le are clear. The compressed dark cluster between them has rounded upper/lower contours and a right upright. Overlapping c/u is plausible, but the original C alternative m cannot be excluded from the degraded strokes. No separate earlier character or chronological correction is established. H gives fascicule without this doubt.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

changes.locus: Body line 8, clipped initial before ie.
changes.evidence: Crop 13: only a tall upright and lower foot of the first glyph survive; its left bowl, if any, is outside the copied area. The shape permits the right side of d or a clipped l. The full ie and period are clear. The usual phrase does not decide the missing contour.
changes.mathematical_consequence: None; correspondence, not a mathematical assertion.

notes.text: The typed heading states Massy le 23.6.1971 and the salutation addresses Verdier. The body expressly says 23 Mai; this visible 3 is not replaced by the 28 mentioned in H’s editorial cross-reference. No other page was consulted.
notes.basis: Observed heading, salutation and body line 1; H note distinguished from source ink.

notes.text: The letter mentions the missing exer 4.10.6 and sending fascicule 1 of the partly clipped SGA 4 to the printer. These numerals are a reference and volume-part designation, not a calculation or proof.
notes.basis: Observed body lines 2–4; no reconstruction of the clipped conditional word.

notes.text: The visible text says the person who typed the text is finishing, will leave on holiday, and Springer is returning the rented machine for lack of other manuscripts. It ends by postponing publication of this fascicule, followed by the partly clipped phrase sine die.
notes.basis: Observed body lines 4–8; English descriptive summary, not a restoration of missing letters.

notes.text: The copied letter is truncated along both vertical sides. H’s bracketed supplies are editorial restorations; the report records retained doubt or missing text without treating every supplied initial as a lexical error. The cancellation after elle is actual source state omitted by H.
notes.basis: Whole image, half a and crops 01–13; source geometry and cancellation observed.

notes.text: The first letter after imprimeur has both a tall upright and rounded lower ink. The compressed cluster in the later fascimle/fascicule likewise remains ambiguous. The reading does not infer a unique correction order from darkness or from the intended sentence.
notes.basis: Observed crops 12 and 14; alternatives are paleographic, not grammatical repair.

notes.text: The closing reads Bien cordialement with no final punctuation or signature visible. Crop 15 confirms the ascender and bowl of d and the ordinary dotted i; no added accent is transcribed. The lower half is otherwise blank except for the archival 12. No mathematical checking was performed.
notes.basis: Half a, crop 15, half b; observation only, check_events intentionally empty.

notation.evidence: Each numeral and dot was read in half a; capitals G/A are ordinary upright type, and the S is clipped. No mathematical alphabet or bold type is established.
notation.alternatives: Only the clipped S remains doubtful.

notation.evidence: Crop 04 shows a separate accent-like top mark over initial e and an ordinary final acute.
Crop 14: l-like ascender/serifs coexist with lower rounded ink; a simple degraded d remains possible.
notation.alternatives: c/l or e/l superposition in either order; d

notation.evidence: Crop 09 shows two crossed cancellation shapes over an unreadable short tail.
notation.alternatives: Underlying letters and any earlier history unresolved.
